chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, and from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Statement of the Exalted: 'Who is he that will Loan to Allah a beautiful loan? for (Allah) will increase it manifold to his credit, and he will have (besides) a liberal Reward', he said: 'It is the 'good' towards the Imam during the government of the mischief'.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of lending to Allah in Surah Al-Hadid according to Imam al-Madi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Madi (peace be upon him) interprets the 'good loan' in Surah Al-Hadid as the financial support or *khums* given to the Imam during the era of the *dawlat al-fasq* (the government of the unjust). This interpretation highlights the Imam's role as the rightful recipient of divine wealth during the Major Occultation, linking material generosity to spiritual reward in a time of political alienation.

en.hubeali: H 14909 – Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Abdullah Bin Al-Salt, from Yunus, and from Abdul Aziz Bin Al-Muhtady, from a man, who has narrated the following: Abu Al-Hassan the Lastasws

regarding the Statement of the High: “[57:11] Who is he that will Loan to Allah a beautiful loan? for (Allah) will increase it manifold to his credit, and he will have (besides) a liberal Reward”, heasws said; ‘It is the ‘good’ towards the Imamasws during the government of the mischief’.
en.sarwar: 462. Yunus, from Sinan Bin Tareyf who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘It is befitting for ‘لِلْمُؤْمِنِ’ the Believer that he should fear Allah (azwj) with such a fear as if he is overlooking upon the Fire, and hope with such a hope as if he is from the inhabitants of the Paradise’.
Then said: ‘Allah (azwj) is with the expectation of His (azwj) servant. If he expects good, so it will be good, and if he expects evil, so it will be evil’.
